English_Example: They sell chives and thyme by the market.

Kweyol_Example: Mété gwo diten-an an sòs-la, i ni an bon gou.
English_Example: Put thyme in the sauce, it has a good flavour.

Kweyol_Example: Si ou pwan wimèd sala, i pa kay fè’w ditò.
English_Example: If you take this medicine, it won’t hurt you.

English_Example: By the market you find various kinds of ground provisions.

Kweyol_Example: Madanm-lan fè mwen ouvè lanmen mwen pou i té sa diviné ban mwen.
English_Example: The woman had me open my hand in order to tell me about my future.

Kweyol_Example: Manman mwen sé on divinè.
English_Example: My mother is a seer.

Kweyol_Example: Tout sé disip-la té apèsivwè divinité Jézi.
English_Example: All of the disciples perceived Jesus’ divinity.

Kweyol_Example: La ni twòp divizyon an fanmi sala.
English_Example: There’s too much division in that family.

Kweyol_Example: Sé moun-an vlé swiv divwa Bondyé.
English_Example: The people wanted to follow God’s will.

Kweyol_Example: Yo koupé kann tousèl pou diwan tan wékòt-la.
English_Example: They cut only cane for the duration of the harvest.

Kweyol_Example: Nou kay viv épi Bondyé pou lavi diwant.
English_Example: We will live with God for eternity.

Kweyol_Example: Dépi sé kon sa ou ka bas, ou pa kay diwé.
English_Example: If you bat like that, you won’t last.

Kweyol_Example: Mwen di’y koté pou i jwenn avoka-a épi i alé la diwèktiman.
English_Example: I told him where to find the lawyer and he went there directly.

Kweyol_Example: Mwen pa sav diwèktiman ki jou papa mwen ka vini.
English_Example: I don’t know exactly what day my father is coming.

Kweyol_Example: Yo ka manjé diwi èk pwa wouj.
English_Example: They’re eating rice and red beans.

Kweyol_Example: Yo kay wèsté la pou dizan.
English_Example: They’ll remain there for 10 years.

Kweyol_Example: La té ni on dja bò kay-la bonmaten- an.
English_Example: There was a wreck by the house this morning.

Kweyol_Example: Gwan moun di lè lapli sòlèy, djab ka mayé dèyè kay.
English_Example: Old folks say that when the sun shines as it is raining, devils are getting married behind the house.

Kweyol_Example: Fanm sa-a sé djabal tonton mwen.
English_Example: That woman is my uncle’s mistress.

Kweyol_Example: Tifi sala sé on bèl djal.
English_Example: This girl is a nice chick.

Kweyol_Example: Fanm sala sé on djanmèt.
English_Example: That woman’s a prostitute.

Definition: a plant that heals, flu, cold and internal injuries when made into a tea.
Kweyol_Example: Tibway-la ni wim, sé pou ou fè dité djapanna ba li.
English_Example: The boy has a cold and you should make djapanna tea for him.

Kweyol_Example: Nou té djé  toubonmnan!

Kweyol_Example: Nou pa té sa jwé bol-la paski la pa té ni djè moun.
English_Example: We couldn’t play ball because there were hardly any people.

Definition: mouth or snout of an animal.

Kweyol_Example: Djèp-la pitjé’y patan i té ka aché mango.
English_Example: The wasp stung him when he was looking for mangoes.

Kweyol_Example: Nou ka mété djèt an tout konwen kay-la.
English_Example: We are putting braces on all the corners of the house.

Definition: to freeload, to expect something that you have not been invited to take.
Kweyol_Example: Pa asiz lakay sé moun-an pou djété pou manjé yo.
English_Example: Don’t sit at their home and expect to eat uninvited.

Kweyol_Example: Dòktè-a djéwi boug-la.
English_Example: The doctor cured the fellow.

Kweyol_Example: Maladi sala pa ni djéwizon.
English_Example: That illness has no remedy.

Kweyol_Example: Ou sa fè nou soufè mé ou pa sa pwan djèwté nou.
English_Example: You can make us suffer but you can’t take away our joy.

Kweyol_Example: Ou kay an djèwté lè gason’w-lan vini sòti lòt péyi.
English_Example: You’ll be joyful when your son comes back from overseas.

Kweyol_Example: Lèswpi Bondyé sé djid nou.
English_Example: The Spirit of God is our guide.

Kweyol_Example: Lè ou alé an souf, la toujou ni on moun pou djidé’w.
English_Example: When you go to the sulphur springs, there is always someone to guide you.

Definition: person with very dark, blue- black skin.

Kweyol_Example: Yo wivé abò on djip.
English_Example: They arrived in a Jeep.

Definition: to run quickly, to run away, to flee.
Kweyol_Example: Vòlè-a fè djip lè i wè polis-la chapé.
English_Example: The thief ran away when he saw the police coming.

Kweyol_Example: Ou ni djiyon paski ou ka twavay toulé jou mé ou pa janmen ni lajan.
English_Example: You have bad luck because you are working every day yet you never have money.

Kweyol_Example: I pèd djòb li tou.
English_Example: He lost his job too.

Definition: mouth or snout of an animal.
Kweyol_Example: I bay bouwik-la an koul wòch asou djòl li.
English_Example: He hit the donkey on the mouth with a stone.

Definition: to run one’s mouth, to speak without anymore paying attention.
Kweyol_Example: Ou sa bat djòl ou kon ou vlé, mwen pa mélé.
English_Example: You can run your mouth all you want, I don't care.

Definition: mouth or opening of a hole.
Kweyol_Example: Tibway-la mété an wòch asou djòl twou kwab-la.
English_Example: The boy put a stone over the opening of the crab hole.

Kweyol_Example: Misyé-a té ni pou alé wè dòktè paski i té ni djòn.
English_Example: The man had to go see the doctor because he had gonorrhoea.

Kweyol_Example: Ti manmay-la pa malad i djòs mové.
English_Example: The child isn’t sick he’s just bad.

Kweyol_Example: Djouk sé on pwéson ki ka santi fwé an chay.
English_Example: Djouk is a kind of fish that smells very rotten.

Definition: a sharp piece of wood, such as the root of a tree that has been cut down, sticking up out of the ground, over which someon might trip or get hurt.
Kweyol_Example: Tibway-la tonbé anlè an djouk bwa épi  djouk bwa-a èstòpyé’y.
English_Example: The boy fell on a sharp piece of wood and it cut him.

Kweyol_Example: Las djouké mwen avan mwen fè on bagay épi’w!

Kweyol_Example: Lè chyen-an bouwé dèyè’y i antwé an kay-la djoup toubonnman.
English_Example: When the dog charged after him, he went straight into the house just like that.

Kweyol_Example: Vè-a plen dlo.
English_Example: The glass is full of water.

Kweyol_Example: Mwen ka di zòt oplèz èk dlo an zyé mwen.

Kweyol_Example: Yo benyen tifi-a an dlo ajenni.
English_Example: They bathed the girl in the fountain of youth.

Kweyol_Example: Pwéson sala pa ka wété an lanmè-a, i ka wété an dlo dous.
English_Example: That fish doesn’t live in the sea, it lives in fresh water.

Definition: gripe water, given to babies for gas.
Kweyol_Example: Yo bay ti manmay-la dlo gwip paski i té ni kolik.
English_Example: They gave the baby gripe water because he had colic.

Kweyol_Example: Nonm sala pa ka mété dlo an bouch li pou di’w anyen.

Definition: sugar water, given to a child as medicine after a fall.

English_Example: The little girl took a sip; we gave her sugar water to drink.

Kweyol_Example: Nonm-lan ka alé lanmè dwi toujou magwé i sé an gwan nonm.
English_Example: The man still goes to the sea often although he’s old.

Definition: someone who wanders aimlessly, loafer, someone who is unproductive.
Kweyol_Example: Tibway sala sé on dwivayèz.
English_Example: That boy is an aimless wanderer.

Kweyol_Example: Yo pa ni anyen pou fè, kon sa yo enmen dwivé tout lajouné-a.
English_Example: They have nothing to do, so they love to stroll all day long.

Definition: a traditional dress worn when dancing the quadrille.

Kweyol_Example: Ès ou vlé sala ében lòt-la?
English_Example: Do you want that or the other?

Kweyol_Example: Ében, fè sa ou vlé.
English_Example: Then do what you want.

Kweyol_Example: Tibway sala toujou ni échofi paski i pa ka lavé pyé’y.
English_Example: That boy always has athlete’s foot because he doesn’t wash his feet.

Kweyol_Example: Sé pou ou viv pa ègzanp.
English_Example: You must live your life as an example for others.

English_Example: The sound of the axe echoed in the forest.

Definition: to clarify, to make clear, to enlighten.

English_Example: Clarify that for me, please.

Kweyol_Example: Apwézan tan-an ékléwé.

Kweyol_Example: Tout zé poul-la éklò.

Kweyol_Example: Lè yo tann sa, yo kay pli ékoutan.

Kweyol_Example: Yo mennen tout bagay èksèpté sa.

English_Example: You won’t be saved unless you know Jesus.

Kweyol_Example: Dòktè-a ka gadé èkstré fwisi misyé-a.

English_Example: The girl was in an accident and they had to x-ray her head.

Definition: to have the ability to write.
